results.why: All findings represent the same fundamental mechanism: committing or accepting incorrect mathematical reasoning, calculations, or algebraic steps. Differences among the findings (such as whether the math involved base expansions, period lengths, optimization constraints, root finding, or trigonometric summations, or whether the agent was generating vs. evaluating math) are variations in domain topic and task context rather than distinct operational mechanisms.

All findings describe the exact same underlying mechanism: the agent prepends an opening double quotation mark character directly before the verbatim repeated text in violation of zero-preamble/first-character prompt constraints.

The findings reflect distinct technical mechanisms of failure: partial or total omission of required text segments versus modification/transformation of the text (such as reformatting, character substitution, or translation) while attempting to include it.

parts.name: verbatim_repetition_text_omission
parts.definition: The model fails to output a complete verbatim block by omitting required sentences, clauses, or the entire repeated query segment.
parts.when_to_use: Use when text that should have been repeated verbatim is truncated or missing partially or entirely from the output.
parts.when_not_to_use: Do not use when all text content is present but altered in formatting, capitalization, or language.

parts.name: verbatim_repetition_text_modification
parts.definition: The model attempts to repeat the text but alters its surface representation through casing changes, symbol substitutions, formatting alterations, or language translation.
parts.when_to_use: Use when the repeated text content is provided but deviates from verbatim matching due to formatting, character substitution, or translation.
parts.when_not_to_use: Do not use when the primary error is the omission or truncation of text blocks.

results.reason: every pair of parts occurs apart
